security_spec.violation_condition: In the Linux kernel, when S-mode writes SPMP CSRs (spmpaddr/spmpcfg via sireg/sireg2/siselect, or sspmpswitch) during a context switch or dynamic reconfiguration and resumes execution of the incoming task without first issuing SFENCE.VMA with rs1=x0 and rs2=x0, subsequent memory accesses from the incoming task may be checked against stale SPMP entries rather than the newly written configuration.
security_spec.summary: SPMP CSR writes are explicitly not ordered with respect to subsequent memory accesses; omitting SFENCE.VMA after SPMP reprogramming allows incoming task to operate under stale SPMP rules, potentially granting unauthorized memory access

findings.finding: SPMP (S-mode Physical Memory Protection) is not implemented in this Linux kernel tree. The siselect/sireg CSRs (0x150/0x151) are defined but used exclusively for KVM AIA IMSIC interrupt controller access, not for SPMP. No sspmpswitch CSR is defined. No SPMP-related writes occur in context-switch paths, signal delivery, or SMP hotplug paths, so the spec's violation condition (writing SPMP CSRs without subsequent SFENCE.VMA) cannot be triggered.
